case_name: National Association of the Deaf v. Harvard University
court: U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts
claim_type: Online lectures, MOOCs, podcasts, and public-facing video content lacked accurate closed captioning
outcome: Class action consent decree settlement approved February 27, 2020; Harvard paid $1.5M+ in attorney fees; required to caption all new public-facing online content and all archived content on request within 5 business days
estimated_defense_cost: Attorney fees awarded exceeded $1.5 million; five years of litigation costs not disclosed separately

summary_one_line: Five-year battle over online course captioning; Harvard paid $1.5M+ in attorney fees and must caption all public-facing online content — a warning for any business with video content.
notes: Companion case: NAD v. MIT (D. Mass. 3:15-cv-30024) settled similarly July 21, 2020. DOJ filed statement of interest supporting plaintiffs June 25, 2015. Settlement requires live captioning at university-wide streamed events. Sets precedent for any business with online video content (webinars, product demos, course content, YouTube).
